title: Barrowlight
intro:
Rain has followed you for three days across the Greywater moor. The villagers of Hollin's Rest would not say the barrow's name. They only pointed north and made the sign of the ash.

Somewhere beneath that mound lies the Barrowlight, the lantern the Ashen Order kept burning so their dead would sleep. It went dark at the turn of the season. Since then, the graves of Hollin's Rest have not stayed shut.

You crest the last hill as dusk bleeds out of the sky, and the lichgate rises before you.

epilogues.text:
Above you, Ser Halric rests at last on his own sarcophagus, his long watch ended. Below you, the Barrowlight burns with a warm, steady gold, and the spiral stair winds down and down through the bedrock until the walls fall away entirely.

The cavern that opens beneath the hill is vast beyond reckoning. A mist of ash and silver moss drifts over sunken roofs and leaning towers, pale lanterns glimmer in windows that should have gone dark centuries ago, and somewhere in the twilight a bell answers the lantern's light. This is no tomb. Something down here is still living.

You chalk the Ashen flame on the last step. Whether Sister Wren is one turning behind you or an hour behind, following your marks into the dark, you know she is coming. The Ashen Order is two people now, {player.name}, and its true work has only just begun.

Ser Halric's last word follows you down the spiral stair: relieved. You walk without Sister Wren's blessing, and no one will chalk a trail behind you. Still, the Barrowlight burns warm and unclouded in your hand, a golden flame that seems to answer the mercy you showed its guardian.

The stair ends at the lip of a chasm so wide that its far side is lost in mist. Below, pale lanterns glimmer among sunken halls and silver moss, and a bell tolls somewhere in the deep, slow as a sleeper's heartbeat.

You did not need a blade to reach this place, {player.name}. Whatever waits in the Under-Barrow, you meet it with clean hands and a clear light.

Ser Halric's shattered armor lies scattered in the ash behind you. The Barrowlight burns in your hand, but its flame is thin and ash-pale, heavy with the memory of steel, as though it has not yet decided whether to forgive the way you won it.

Yet Wren believed in you, and her faith steadies your hand on the long spiral down. When the stair finally opens onto the vast twilight of the Under-Barrow, with its drowned roofs and drifting ash, you stop and say a prayer for the knight you could not save. Far off, the subterranean bells answer.

You chalk the Order's flame on the stone for Wren to follow, {player.name}, and walk on into the deep.

Above you, the lichgate stands empty, Wren's bedroll sodden in the mud, and Halric's bones lie broken in the ash of the Barrow Heart. In your grip the Barrowlight burns cold and pale as frost, giving light but no warmth.

You descend alone. The spiral stair goes down far longer than it should, and when it ends, the dark beneath the hill opens like an indrawn breath: endless, echoing, and not empty. Somewhere out in that black, older things are waking to the sound of your footsteps.

No one will follow your trail, {player.name}. No one even knows to.

With Ser Halric fallen and the Barrowlight awake in your hand, you leave the upper crypt behind and follow the hidden stair down into the earth. The lantern's flame is a thin, uncertain thing, but it is enough to light the next step, and the next.

At the bottom the stair opens onto a subterranean dark so vast that your light cannot find its edges. Somewhere out there lie the sunken halls of the first sleepers, and the true secrets of Greywater's dead wait for you in the deep, {player.name}.

gameOverText: The cold of the barrow closes over you like deep water. Somewhere far above, rain falls on the lichgate, and the Barrowlight stays dark. Your story ends here, {player.name}.
